brief: Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities strategist Faris Mourad argues the current bout of AI pessimism is overdone and recommends buying the dip in the AI hardware basket GSTMTDAT. The chain: geopolitical escalation, midterm elections and the Fed decision raise macro uncertainty, so the desk prefers secular growth themes with little economic sensitivity over the next 12 months. AI fundamentals support this, with OpenAI's Astra model lifting AI-linked stocks, AVGO reaffirming FY27/28 AI revenue targets of $115B/$230B against constrained supply, and CSCO citing a 5x rise in network bandwidth consumption from agentic AI. Prime brokerage data shows positioning cleaned up: the AI Hardware basket long/short ratio sits at the 51st percentile over one year and 83rd over three, AI Power at the 4th and 14th. Post-unwind conviction is directionless, so basket exposure beats stock-picking. Separately, the Democratic ratepayer-protection agenda would shift AI power costs onto datacenters, helping utilities and grid operators while hurting datacenter project economics. Broad AI versus S&P ex-AI is up about 17% off the local lows.
